title: festuca idahoensis subsp. roemeri
intro: Festuca idahoensis subsp. roemeri, commonly known as Roemer's fescue, is a plant species belonging to the family Poaceae. It is a perennial grass native to North America, often used in traditional medicine for its potential health benefits. The plant has been reported to have anti-inflammatory, antioxidant, and antimicrobial properties, making it a promising natural remedy for various health issues. The bioactive constituents of Roemer's fescue include flavonoids, phenolic acids, and essential oils, which are believed to contribute to its therapeutic actions.
